passage:
During a home repair, Sam found old newspapers under the floor. They were used many years ago to protect the wood.
The paper was yellow and easy to tear. Sam and his father read the headlines carefully. Some stories seemed serious at the time but were now forgotten. Others were about changes that still affected the city.
Sam noticed old advertisements for products that no longer existed. He laughed at the prices.
His father said, "A newspaper is written for one day, but later it becomes history."
Sam put the best pages in a folder. Yesterday's news had become a window into a world that had not expected to be studied.
